Pruning based on posterior probability now works and improves mismatch rate on test data (although doing so appears to increase switch error rate?) Priors for different genotypes are hardcoded currently, so reading these from the input VCF needs to be added. commit message:
Add support for a precomputed distance matrix. Unfortunately, this seems to be much less efficient than one might think, unless we're using a rather expensive distance function, or we're using clever tricks to accelerate this (which we are not yet; but might as well do for e.g. Euclidean distance).
Precomputing a distance matrix for 10k objects: 31 sec. PAM k=10 runtime: +264 sec (36 iterations). without: 351 sec, i.e. 15% faster only.

fix(generate.py): use Decimal to correctly report conversion factors

To display correct conversion values, we limit the precision context to
2 places (required by Hz). Higher precisions, such as the default
machine precision, include the usual issues with floating point
arithmetic and do not display exact conversions.

References:
- https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/floatingpoint.html
- https://docs.python.org/3/library/decimal.html#module-decimal

Fixes https://github.com/NeuroML/NeuroML2/issues/134

feat(schema): add simple type to restrict component reference paths

The regex says that the path must be a string that:

- may start with a `/`
- followed by any number of the following strings optionally suffixed
  with a `/`
  - `../`
  - `./`
  - `[0-9]`
  - a string with the first letter as an alphanumberic letter, followed
    by any number of alphanumeric + `_` letters

commit message:
New pre-release 1.0.2-9

- Data for station locations and unique identifiers is now provided
with the package on installation. Previously this was fetched each time
from the ftp server.
- The station metadata can now be updated if necessary by using
`get_station_list()`, this change overwrites the internal data that
were originally distributed with the package. This operation will fetch
the latest list of stations and corresponding information from the NCEI
ftp server. Any changes will be overwritten when the R package is
updated, however,
the package update should have the same or newer data included, so this
should not be an issue.

commit message:
Bugfixes and enhancements

If a station or several stations are queried, the function now checks
the years that NCDC reports stations having data and gives an error
message if outside this range.

In some cases, this is inaccurate or files simply do not exist. If this
is the case, the function simply moves on and silently fails when there
are no files to ftp from NCDC. That is, if a file is requested that
does not exist, the function returns a message.

`nearest_stations()` is now functional

Update documentation for all functions and files

Added RCUrl to dependencies

Fixed typos in fetch_isd-history.Rmd

Update vignette with more examples, especially using
`nearest_stations()`

country

commit message:
Provide only SRTM 90m elevation data

Rather than providing our own version of the isd-history.csv file,
instead we will provide a data frame that includes only a STNID to join
the CGIAR_SRTM elevation data column with the idd-history.csv file,
which will be fetched when running the `get_GSOD()` function.

This means that the latest data for the stations should be available
including the dates available, new stations coming online, etc. without
the need for frequent updates to the R package. New stations come
online much less frequently, which mean that the elevation values do
not need to be updated as often.

This negates the need for the "refresh" option in `get_GSOD()` as well.

commit message:
lint files

More detailed explanatory text, if necessary. Wrap it to about 72
characters or so. In some contexts, the first line is treated as the
subject of the commit and the rest of the text as the body. The
blank line separating the summary from the body is critical (unless
you omit the body entirely); various tools like `log`, `shortlog`
and `rebase` can get confused if you run the two together.

Explain the problem that this commit is solving. Focus on why you
are making this change as opposed to how (the code explains that).
Are there side effects or other unintuitive consequences of this
change? Here's the place to explain them.

Further paragraphs come after blank lines.

 - Bullet points are okay, too

 - Typically a hyphen or asterisk is used for the bullet, preceded
   by a single space, with blank lines in between, but conventions
   vary here

If you use an issue tracker, put references to them at the bottom,
like this:

Resolves: #123
See also: #456, #789

commit message:
Add CRU CL2.0 Data; Update data sources;

Adding climate data from CRU CL2.0:
Mark New (1,*), David Lister (2), Mike Hulme (3), Ian Makin (4)

A high-resolution data set of surface climate over global land areas
Climate Research, 2000, Vol 21, pg 1-25

School of Geography and the Environment, University of Oxford,
Mansfield Road, Oxford OX1 3TB, United Kingdom
Climatic Research Unit, and (3) Tyndall Centre for Climate Change
Research, both at School of Environmental Sciences, University of East
Anglia, Norwich NR4 7TJ, United Kingdom
International Water Management Institute, PO Box 2075, Colombo, Sri
Lanka
ABSTRACT: We describe the construction of a 10-minute
latitude/longitude data set of mean monthly surface climate over global
land areas, excluding Antarctica. The climatology includes 8 climate
elements - precipitation, wet-day frequency, temperature, diurnal
temperature range, relative humidity,sunshine duration, ground frost
frequency and windspeed - and was interpolated from a data set of
station means for the period centred on 1961 to 1990. Precipitation was
first defined in terms of the parameters of the Gamma distribution,
enabling the calculation of monthly precipitation at any given return
period. The data are compared to an earlier data set at 0.5 degrees
latitude/longitude resolution and show added value over most regions.
The data will have many applications in applied climatology,
biogeochemical modelling, hydrology and agricultural meteorology and
are available through the School of Geography Oxford
(http://www.geog.ox.ac.uk), the International Water Management
Institute "World Water and Climate Atlas" (http://www.iwmi.org) and the
Climatic Research Unit (http://www.cru.uea.ac.uk).

Also updating country list and SRTM elevation data

commit message:
#1712 "Bode plot: linear frequency axis wish is ignored" #1713 "Issues for large systems with large eigenvalues/Zeros" fixed. Furthermore, several improvements made: - New function StateSpace.Transformation.toBalancedForm Performs a similarity transformation to a balanced form. The goal is to make further numerical computations on the system more reliable. - Improved functions
ModelAnalysis.Poles ModelAnalysis.Zeros ModelAnalysis.FullAnalysis StateSpace.Plot.polesAndZeros System is now balanced, before eigenvalues and transmission zeros are computed (to improve numerics for systems with largely varying zeros and poles). - Improved functions ModelAnalysis.TransferFunctions StateSpace.Plot.bodeSISO StateSpace.Plot.bodeMIMO System is now balanced, before bode plot is computed (to improve numerics for systems with largely varying zeros and poles). For large systems with large eigenvalues or zeros, an overflow could occur. The algorithm has been changed so that overflow is much more unlikely to occur. The computation of the bode plot is now 1-2 orders of magnitudes faster for large systems (the implementation of the algorithm was restructured and part of the restructured functionality is now pre-compiled in object code using the __Dymola_translate=true annotation. Optionally, it is now possible to store the frequency, magnitude and angle vectors of the bode diagram on file. - Bug fix in StateSpace.Plot.bodeSISO StateSpace.Plot.bodeMIMO ZerosAndPoles.Plot.bode Defining logX=false, still computed the frequency vector in logarithmic scale (and f_min=0 gave an error). This has been fixed. If a system had many zeros and poles with large absolute values, an overflow could occur. The algorithm has been changed to make this situation much more unlikely. git-svn-id: https://svn.modelica.org/projects/Modelica_EmbeddedSystems/trunk/Modelica_LinearSystems2@8204 7ce873d0-865f-4ce7-a662-4bb36ea78beb

Fix of #847 "Repeated use of linearization issue"
Based on a suggestion by Hans, a "translateModel" is added at the end of the linearizations. Since the model is already translated, this call will not re-translated. However, it resets the dsin.txt file. Calling linearization several times with the same linearization time instant t > 0.0, gives now the same results (before this fix, different results could have been obtained).

commit message:
Bugs fixed:
- Modelica_LinearSystems2.StateSpace.Analysis.invariantZeros:
  When large invariant zeros are present, these have been wrongly set to zero
  (indirectly to avoid a division by zero). This has been corrected:
  The pencil (Af,Bf) has n eigenvalues (= the invariant zeros). 
  The transformation to this form is performed so that Bf is regular.
  Therefore, the generalized eigenvalues represented by alpha[i]/beta[i] have the
  property that beta[i] cannot be zero and a division by beta[i] is uncritical.
  The fix was to removed the inapproiate algorithm to avoid a division by a zero
  beta[i]. As a side effect, large transmission zeros are no longer set to zero.

- Modelica_LinearSystems2.StateSpace.Internal.reduceRosenbrock:
  This function contains code to determine the rank of several systems.
  The "eps" used for the rank determination was wrongly set to norm(A)*1e-12
  which gives an in appropriate values if the norm of A is small, but of B and/or C
  large. This was changed to:
    eps = norm([A,B;C,D])*Modelica.Constants.eps*1000

- Modelica_LinearSystems2.Math.Polynomial.'String'
  The String overloaded operator returned a wrong string resprentation
  of a polynomial if one or more leading coefficients are zero.
  This has been corrected.

- Modelica_LinearSystems2.StateSpace.Analysis.analysis
  The default number of significant digits to print the A,B,C,D matrix elements
  was changed from 3 to 6.

fix(dagre): Fixed the error positions of nodes with dagre layout.

The G6/ dagre layout uses the original index of nodes to set the {x, y}.

But in dagre.js, the g.nodes() and g.edges() return arrays not the same order with out original nodes and edges.

So we should use the node.id and edge.source+edge.target to get the original model to set their positions.

commit message:
更新bundle.zh.md (#7431)

* 更新bundle.zh.md

vue-cli会在合并webpack配置项之前，为webpack配置项mode按开发态、生产态自动赋值。

重点是：在开发态下，开发者反复修改代码并触发构建行为时，会因为mode: 'production'这个配置状态激发的webpack在依赖缓存目录下预先缓存TerserWebpackPlugin导致运行时大小过大而重新构建耗时过长效果，影响开发体验。

所以如果不是使用原生webpack直接构建工程而是使用的vue-cli，需要这句话。

* Update packages/site/docs/manual/further-reading/bundle.zh.md

commit message:
refactor: optimize plugin export architecture and canvas rendering

- Plugin Export Architecture Improvements:
  - Add public getPluginInstances() method to PluginController
  - Replace fragile internal property access with stable public API
  - Remove tight coupling between Graph and DOM elements

- Canvas Export Rendering Enhancements:
  - Replace unreliable setTimeout with deterministic waitForRenderingComplete()
  - Use requestAnimationFrame for reliable rendering completion detection
  - Improve export reliability and performance

- Background Plugin Export Optimizations:
  - Fix transparency handling to support transparent background export
  - Correct 'auto' keyword handling in background-size calculations
  - Support complex CSS background-size values like '100px auto', 'auto 50%'

- Error Handling Improvements:
  - Add proper error logging for plugin rendering failures
  - Improve debugging experience with detailed error messages

- Runtime Context Management:
  - Add direct runtime context setting/getting methods to Canvas
  - Remove fragile __g6_graph_instance__ DOM property dependency
  - Improve architecture robustness and maintainability

These optimizations enhance the reliability, maintainability,
and CSS compliance of the plugin export functionality.

fix(dagre): Fixed the error positions of nodes with dagre layout.

The G6/ dagre layout uses the original index of nodes to set the {x, y}.

But in dagre.js, the g.nodes() and g.edges() return arrays not the same order with out original nodes and edges.

So we should use the node.id and edge.source+edge.target to get the original model to set their positions.

Fixed #1032

commit message:
更新bundle.zh.md

vue-cli会在合并webpack配置项之前，为webpack配置项mode按开发态、生产态自动赋值。

重点是：在开发态下，开发者反复修改代码并触发构建行为时，会因为mode: 'production'这个配置状态激发的webpack在依赖缓存目录下预先缓存TerserWebpackPlugin导致运行时大小过大而重新构建耗时过长效果，影响开发体验。

所以如果不是使用原生webpack直接构建工程而是使用的vue-cli，需要这句话。

commit message:
perf(layout): 缓存布局模拟结果，避免重复计算

问题描述：
初次渲染时 preLayout 和 preLayoutDraw 分别调用 simulate 进行布局模拟，
导致相同的布局计算执行两次，造成性能浪费。

优化方案：
- 在 LayoutController 中新增 simulationCache 字段缓存 simulate 结果
- preLayout 执行 simulate 后缓存结果
- preLayoutDraw 优先使用缓存，避免重复调用
- 使用完成后立即清除缓存，确保下次渲染时重新计算

性能提升：
- 初次渲染耗时减少约 50%（避免重复布局计算）
- 内存占用增加可忽略（仅临时缓存，使用后立即清除）

新增 API：
- getCachedSimulation(): 获取缓存的布局模拟结果
- clearSimulationCache(): 清除布局模拟缓存

相关 Issue: #7439

commit message:
Merge branch 'master' into hmf

* master:
  undoing previous modifications
  added angular comoving distance with curvature (fixed luminosity distance)
  make swig unnecessary
  small bugs
  Vastly simplify setup.py by getting swig to just link against the installed libccl C library. BREAKAGE: This introduces a new variable in setup.py called LIBCCL_LIBRARY_PATH. This must be filled by autotools with the eventual installed location of the libccl library. This has not been done yet though, so the installer is currently broken.
  Add support for dNdz_tomog in pyccl, including user-defined photo-z functions. This involves some slightly delicate C/Python callback handling, to allow CCL to call a user-defined Python function (wrapped in a PhotoZFunction object).
  Remove obsolete testing file
  Add -std=gnu99 to make for loop int declarations valid and to ensure that M_PI is defined (thanks to David Alonso)
  Add array length checking assertions in ccl_background.i, to match what is done in other modules
  Remove commented-out code
  * Modify setup.py to install supporting data for CLASS (into the same    install dir as the Python files).  * Set __CLASSDIR__ variable at compile-time to allow CLASS to find the data.  * Ignore autogenerated swig source files and build directories
  Print useful information when a Parameters object is printed
  Fix setup.py and remove autogenerated file
  * Split swig interface out into separate interface files  * Wrap most functions to allow numpy vectorisation  * Manually structure interface with __init__ file (direct swig interface    is imported and available through pyccl.lib)  * Wrap C structures in (idiomatic) Python objects  * Get CLASS functions to build via swig
  Comment out unimplemented power spectrum fn as this trips up swig
  Ignore python pyc files
  Include initial numpy array handling support
  Clunky initial implementation of swig Python bindings

commit message:
Use a flatter include structure and avoid 'pragma once'

see #466.

Most public API are in ccl.h, except a few optional ones in:

ccl_emu17, ccl_halomod and ccl_lsst_specs;

on the inter-header dependency:

internal code also directly includes ccl.h to avoid tracking inter
header dependency.

if a module is included in ccl.h, then the only file that tracks this dependency is
ccl.h. otherwise a little bit of care is needed to include the headers
in ccl_emu17, ccl_halomod and ccl_lsst_specs.

I did find it a bit strange that ccl_power depends on ccl_emu17. Refactoring is possible,
but at a cost of backward compatibility and verboseness of the API.

commit message:
SurveySimulation: attributes and methods partially reshaped

Completeness and BrownCompleteness:
- completeness_update arguments (TL, sInd, obsbegin, obsend, nexttime)
—> (TL, sInds, dt)

OpticalSystem:
- detection (0 or 1) —> detectionMode (True or False)
- occulter (0 or 1) —> occulter (True or False)

Post_processing:
- new maxFAfluxratio (float, callable WA-dependent): Maximum flux ratio
that can be obtained by a false alarm. Defaults to 1e-6.

SimulatedUniverse:
- gen_planetary_systems —> gen_physical_properties (no output, but
generates nPlans, plan2star, sInds, a, e, I, O, w, M0, p, Rp, Mp)
- planet_pos_vel_ez —> init_systems (no output, but generates r, v, d,
s, phi, fEZ, dMag, WA, planTime)
- prop_systems —> propag_systems (no output, but updates r, v, d, s,
phi, fEZ, dMag, WA, planTime)

SurveySimulation attributes:
- attribute spectra —> fullSpectra and partialSpectra
- renamed lists: starVisits, starTimes, starRevisit, starExtended
- new attribute: lastDetected (float nx4 ndarray): For each target,
contains 4 lists with planets' detected status, exozodi brightness (in

commit message:
Major update to SurveySimulation prototype

Major update to SurveySimulation prototype

- new attribute: charMargin (float) Integration time margin for
characterization, default to 25%
- new attribute: seed (integer) Random seed used to make all random
number generation reproducible.  This seed is created in MissionSim and
passed through the specs dictionary. (addressing #49)
- update to _outspec: now storing seed. Also storing WAint and dMagint
as single values. The specific KnownRVSurvey stores WAint and dMagint
full arrays (addressing #50)
- default WAint set to (IWA+OWA)/2 or 2*IWA if OWA is infinite
(addressing #48)
- DRM standardized: all arrays are numpy ndarrays or astropy quantity
arrays for outputs with units (addressing #54)
- DRM attributes renamed to det_* char_* and FA_*
- det_status and char_status always integers (addressing #52)
